headline.survivors: About 7 in 100 molecules that reach a first human trial are ever approved.
headline.years: Roughly 14 years from the first screen to a prescription.

totalCostNote: the capitalised cost of one approval, counting every failure paid for along the way

stages.name: Discovery
stages.detail: Screening libraries for something that touches the target at all

stages.name: Preclinical
stages.detail: Cells and animals — is it safe enough to give a person?

stages.name: Phase 1
stages.detail: Tens of healthy volunteers. Does it hurt anyone?

stages.name: Phase 2
stages.detail: Hundreds of patients. Does it do anything? Most drugs die here

stages.name: Phase 3
stages.detail: Thousands of patients, hundreds of sites, most of the money

stages.name: Regulatory review
stages.detail: The filing. By this point almost everything gets through

sources: Phase transition rates and the 6.7% likelihood of approval from Phase 1: industry analyses of clinical development success rates reported in 2025 (pharmaphorum / Norstella, drawing on Citeline data).
Capitalised cost of $2.6B per approved drug: DiMasi et al., Tufts Center for the Study of Drug Development (2014) — $1,395M out-of-pocket plus $1,163M in capital costs over the development period.
Stage durations are the ranges routinely quoted by FDA and industry; they vary widely by disease area.
